question: The electron concentration in an n-type semiconductor is the same as hole concentration in a p-type semiconductor. An external field (electric) is applied across each of them. Compare the currents in them.

options.text: No current will flow in p-type, current will only flow in n-type.
current in n-type = current in p-type.
current in p-type > current in n-type.
current in n-type > current in p-type.

solution:
The current is $I = neAv_d = neA\mu E$. The carrier concentrations are equal, but electrons have a higher mobility than holes ($\mu_e > \mu_h$).

So the current in the n-type semiconductor is greater.
